content.title: Arctic Frost | United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary
content.text: Arctic Frost was the vehicle by which partisan FBI agents and DOJ prosecutors could improperly investigate the entire Republican political apparatus. Worse than Watergate Jack Smith’s failed election case against President Trump began at the Biden Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) under the codename “Arctic Frost.” The Biden Department of Justice (DOJ) was out to get President Trump. But that’s not all.Chairman Grassley’s oversight has revealed that hundreds of Republicans were targeted as part of the Arctic Frost investigation – including over a dozen members of Congress and 400+ Republican organizations and individuals.Based on the evidence to-date, Arctic Frost and related weaponization by federal law enforcement under Biden was arguably worse than Watergate. Learn more about what Chairman Grassley and the Senate Judiciary Committee have uncovered: The Evolution and Expansion of Arctic Frost February 14, 2022: FBI Assistant Special Agent in Charge (ASAC) Timothy Thibault sends a draft Arctic Frost opening electronic communication to subordinate FBI agents, including subordinate Special Agent Michelle Ball. Chairman Grassley's office was told that she and Special Agent Jamie Garman were handpicked by Thibault to work on Arctic Frost in order for Thibault to conceal his role as a case initiating agent. This action violated the FBI’s no self-approval rule. February 22, 2022: Thibault provides update that he’s working to get DOJ and FBI HQ to approve a case on the Trump campaign et al "for conspiring to defraud the US Govt via the elector case."The email makes clear the case will be assigned to CR-15, the dismantled FBI Washington Field Office public corruption unit, and discusses putting a team together, including Special Agent Michelle Ball, as well as adding Special Agent Jamie Garman because "her background as an [Assistant U.S. Attorney] will be particularly helpful." February 24, 2022: Thibault emails John Crabb, a prosecutor in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, saying, “I had a discussion with the case team and we believe there to be predication to include former President of the United States Donald J. Trump as a predicated subject.” April 4, 2022 Attorney General Merrick Garland, Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and FBI Director Christopher Wray provide formal sign off to open the case that would become Arctic Frost. April 13, 2022: ARCTIC FROST OFFICIALLY OPENED July 18, 2022: Chairman Grassley writes to Attorney General Garland and Director Wray to amplify whistleblower concerns "about a pattern of clear political partisanship by Thibault as well as other senior FBI and Justice Department officials." Grassley’s letter also references Thibault’s openly partisan conduct on social media. This marked the formal start of Grassley’s investigation into Arctic Frost."[T]he information I have received reveals that Thibault’s political partisanship…impacted his official decision-making on sensitive public corruption investigations… Thibault's partisanship likely affected investigations briefed to, and approved by, senior Justice Department and FBI officials." November 18, 2022: Attorney General Garland appoints Jack Smith as Special Counsel. Fall 2022 – Spring 2023 Jack Smith issues subpoenas for at least twenty members of Congress and hundreds of organizations and individuals. All Republicans. The subpoenas sought broad, extensive and invasive financial data from Republican groups, as well as communications with the media and the legislative branch. August 1, 2023: Jack Smith indicts President Trump on charges of election conspiracy, based off “findings” from Arctic Frost. January 19,2024 Timothy Thibault is found to have violated the Hatch Act for anti-Trump political conduct while at the FBI. July 1, 2024: The Supreme Court clarifies that the Constitution grants presidents immunity for official acts taken while in office, thereby requiring substantial portions of the Jack Smith indictment to be reevaluated. November 5, 2024: President Trump is elected in a historic landslide victory. January 30, 2025 Chairman Grassley and Sen. Ron Johnson (R-Wis.) release the first Arctic Frost records, obtained via whistleblowers, at Kash Patel’s nomination hearing.
